articles.title: PlayStation Reportedly Polling Game Developers After Decision to Kill Discs Sparks Backlash
articles.summary: PlayStation is reportedly sending a lengthy survey to game developers with a question about how they sell physical games after their decision to stop producing physical game discs prompted intense backlash.
body: The death of physical discs will not happen quietly; fans are making their voices heard as loudly as possible, to the point where PlayStation itself is reportedly reaching out to game developers asking for their thoughts on the divisive subject.

Speaking on the Broken Silicon Podcast, content creator, writer, and showrunner Tom claimed that he’d been made aware of a survey making the rounds among game developers from Sony. His sources claimed that it was possibly the longest survey that Sony has ever distributed.

“There is a survey Sony sent out to developers that is, what I was told by my contacts, a bigger survey than they’ve sent almost ever before, if not ever before. And there was a question in it basically trying to ask in a not-direct way, ‘Is there an issue with how we sell games physically?’ or something, like asking developers for feedback on killing discs.

“ Wolverine is still selling plenty of physical copies, and you’ve also got Sony starting to ask devs if they are worried about killing physical [discs], suggesting they realize that if they got a bunch of feedback, maybe they would consider some sort of mea culpa on it. We’ll see.”

articles.title: The Gigabyte A16 Pro 16" RTX 5070 Ti Gaming Laptop Drops to $1,449 During Walmart's GeForce Week Sale
articles.summary: Walmart's GeForce Week Sale is ending soon, but there's still time to pick up a great deal on a powerful gaming laptop. For a limited time, Walmart has the Gigabyte A16 Pro 16" RTX 5070 Ti Gaming Laptop for just $1,449.00 with free shipping.
body: The Gigabyte A16 Pro laptop measures 0.77" at its thinnest point and weighs just 5 pounds, which is light for a 16" gaming laptop. It's equipped with a 16" 2560x1600 165Hz IPS display, Intel Core 7 240H CPU, Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 Ti 12GB GPU with 115W TGP, 32GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD. The Intel Core 7 240H is a 10-core CPU with a max turbo frequency of 5.2GHz. This is a solid, efficient processor for gaming. The RAM is not user upgradeable so it's good that the system already includes 32GB pre-installed. The SSD, on the other hand, is user-upgradeable.

The RTX 5070 Ti mobile GPU performs about 20%-30% better than the RTX 5070. Compared to Nvidia's previous generation RTX 4000 mobile GPUs, it's comparable in performance to the RTX 4080 and pulls ahead of it in games that support DLSS 4.5 and multi-frame generation. The A16 Pro's 5070 Ti GPU is throttled down to 115W TGP instead of the usual 140W max in order to cut down on heat, but it's powerful enough to run most games smoothly on the display's 1600p resolution from classic favs like League of Legends, Roblox, or Fortnite to new releases like Onimusha: Way of the Sword.

articles.title: In Saraab: Beyond The Veil, Your Inner Demons Are Coming For You This November
articles.summary: Anyone looking for a creepy adventure to play in November will want to check out Saraab: Beyond the Veil. Solo developer Lubna Ahmed has announced a November 3 release date for the game on PC via Steam and Itch.io, and a demo will be available for it during the October edition of Steam Next Fest.
body: An Arabian folklore-inspired horror visual-novel game, Saraab follows Elham, a schoolgirl whose brother has suddenly been kidnapped. Rescuing your sibling means confronting your own inner demons, who have been externalized as monsters born of Elham's own psyche. To overcome them, she'll have to unlock the powers of her bloodline and uncover the truth of who she truly is.

"I'm incredibly excited to bring this story to players and share a world shaped by authentic cultural themes, folklore, and emotional experiences that are rarely explored in games," Ahmed said in a press statement. "I hope players everywhere can connect with the game's story and characters, because ultimately, it's a story about the human heart."

articles.title: Arc Raiders Is Testing a PvE Mode Very Soon
articles.summary: Embark Studios has announced that it will be testing a PvE mode for Arc Raiders next month. From October 13 to October 20, Arc Raiders will have a PvE toggle, allowing you to seamlessly switch between lobbies where you can fight other players and lobbies where players can't do damage to you.
body: Embark will be monitoring the player economy and matchmaking times during this period. The team has noted that "it's possible that this will not work," meaning PvE may not actually make its way into the game permanently. This is a test to see how well they can make it'll operate, rather than some kind of stress test.

"It’s important to mention that this is not a risk-free test," said the studio. "The first, unlaunched iteration of ARC Raiders was conceived as a PvE game, and we have been hesitant to return to that concept. There is a risk that introducing a PvE matchmaking toggle could reduce some of the tension that the game was built around. At the same time, we have to respect that some players want to enjoy the game in their own way, and we can’t ignore what the data is telling us.

"As creators, we design a game with an intention for how we think it should be played; but after launch, it becomes the players’ game. This is one of the unique and wonderful things about making games; we build something with a specific vision, and then we get to see players finding their own ways to enjoy it."

articles.title: Ubisoft Almost Made a Zelda Game With Ganondorf as the Protagonist
articles.summary: Ubisoft Milan reportedly pitched a Zelda game to Nintendo that would have taken place in a new universe with a totally different protagonist, but the plan fell through, leading to one of the biggest what-ifs in gaming history.
body: Insider Gaming’s Tom Henderson says the project was internally titled Goliath, so as to appropriately echo the size and scale of what Ubisoft Milan hoped to achieve with the game. It was an ambitious plan, and one that former Ubisoft developer Gian Marco Zanna described as a “new big bang in the video game universe.”

This description, while dramatic, is accurate; Ubisoft Milan’s Zelda game would have been drastically different from anything we’ve seen from the series thus far. Rather than following Link’s adventures in the wilds of Hyrule, it would have been a spin-off title in the broader Zelda universe featuring a brand-new, “never-before-seen character.”

However, during its early concept phase, Nintendo reportedly asked that this protagonist be changed to the franchise’s ultimate big bad: Ganondorf. This would have been the first time Ganondorf was the central, playable character in a Zelda game, and on paper, it sounds like a fantastic idea… but unfortunately, it didn’t end up coming to fruition.

articles.summary: Madden, the David O. Russell-directed John Madden biopic starring Nic Cage, got its first full-length trailer today, and to be completely honest, I have no idea what to make of this movie.
body: The trailer, which shows some of John Madden's time as the head coach of the Raiders before shifting to broadcasting, gives us a very good look at the makeup and prosthetics that turned Nic Cage into the most famous NFL broadcaster of all time. Does he look like John Madden? No, but he does look like Nic Cage wearing John Madden's face as his own, so perhaps this is a secret sequel to Face/Off.

Madden's name is borderline synonymous with football video games today, and we get a brief look at how the game-development process began. This includes John Mulaney as EA founder Trip Hawkins, and we see how Madden was not interested in the original prototype, as it didn't feature 11 players on a team.

articles.title: Nintendo Reportedly Canceled A Ubisoft-Developed Zelda Game Starring Ganondorf
articles.summary: Zelda fans have had no shortage of new games to play in recent years, but it appears that one game--starring the franchise's iconic villain--was also in the works at one point. Rather than having Nintendo internally develop the game, however, the project was in the works at Ubisoft.
body: In a September 24 report, Insider Gaming says that Ubisoft Milan was working on a Zelda spin-off with the internal name "Goliath," which was set to star a new protagonist. During the early period of development, this was changed to have longtime big bad Ganondorf be the playable character. Outside of the Super Smash Bros. series, this would be a first and would presumably be quite different from other Zelda games.

However, the report says that Nintendo "rejected the prototype" back in late 2023, and the team--including Davide Soliani, who directed the Mario + Rabbids games--opted to leave Ubisoft and form their own studio, Day 4 Night, which is currently developing Bradley the Badger. This occurred despite Ubisoft's attempts to pitch Nintendo on a different IP in its place, with both Star Fox and Mario mentioned, but it wasn't meant to be.
It isn't the first time a Zelda spin-off has been canceled, apparently, with Retro Studios' Sheik-focused Project X reportedly getting canned during the Wii's lifespan.

articles.title: Steam’s Punk Games Showcase Hates AI Slop, Loves Blowing Up Nazis
articles.summary: Punks are taking over Steam starting on October 9 with the Punk Games Showcase, a week-long, curated digital festival celebrating games made with and expressing a punk spirit.
body: Over 400 games were submitted for consideration, and the final list includes over 100, with the intention of filtering out any that included generative AI, among other factors. Many featured games have already been released, while others are still to come. A few of them are even out this month or during the event.

Brad Smith of studio Miracle Tea, the creators of Club Soko, has been involved in itch.io's Hardcore Punk Jam since 2018, and is organizing the Steam showcase that will run alongside the game jam's latest edition.

Smith said the showcase has a few simple goals: to highlight games that "feature this style of music, are about the subculture, or are from creators who understand this scene, and it shows significantly in their games." He also hopes the showcase will influence Valve to add a "punk" categorization label on Steam, so developers can tag their games accordingly and players can find them more easily.
I caught up with Smith for more insight into the upcoming showcase and the movement to uplift games that wear their punk roots.

articles.title: Over the Hill Is the Perfect Replacement For Forza Horizon
articles.summary: Over the Hill, an off-road exploration game, is in many ways the anti-Forza Horizon. It's minimalist and chill to the point of mindfulness. It's just you in your chunky little 4x4, roving around a rugged wilderness because it's there.
body: Listen, I love Forza Horizon 6, but it's a lot. It's a lot of content even before you're trying to keep up with the (excellent) weekly Festival Playlist. It's a lot of cars, a lot of notifications, a lot of options, a lot of rewards, a lot of other players. It's noisy. So Over the Hill is perfect counterprogramming — if you can call it counterprogramming when it's also about driving customizable vehicles around gorgeous landscapes.

Over the Hill comes from Funselektor Labs (assisted by Strelka Games), the developer of the impeccably stylish retro rally game Art of Rally. Over the Hill shares Art of Rally 's unlicensed but deliciously toylike renditions of classic cars from the late 20th century, like the Land Rover Defender (Protector), Toyota Land Cruiser (Roamer), and Mercedes G-Wagon (Sentinel). But Over the Hill is no kind of racing game. It's purely about traversal and exploration, about reading the landscape and navigating your way through it.
points: Over the Hill, an off-road exploration game, is in many ways the anti-Forza Horizon.
It's minimalist and chill to the point of mindfulness.
It's just you in your chunky little 4x4, roving around a rugged wilderness because it's there.

Two decades after Sword Saint Isshin Ashina reclaimed the region in a brutal coup, a new threat emerges from within: The Interior Ministry. Desperate to protect his homeland, Isshin’s grandson Genichiro turns to forbidden powers. The only hope lies in a kidnapped boy — the Divine Heir — and his silent protector: a loyal shinobi known only as Sekiro.

Is that also a reason to try it? It did catch my attention, mainly because I find these particular dog people a bit unsettling. I felt the same way about Fox in the Star Fox remake.

articles.title: The Division's New Release is Going Up Against Zelda
articles.summary: The Division 2 is about to send players to one of New York City's most recognizable locations, and it's doing so at almost exactly the same time that Nintendo is sending players back to Hyrule.
body: On Thursday, Ubisoft announced that The Division 2: Echoes of Central Park will launch on Nov. 3, just two days before The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time arrives on Nintendo Switch 2 on Nov. 5. So while Link is preparing to save Hyrule once again, Division agents will be heading into a very different kind of legendary forest.
Ubisoft showed off the DLC in a new gameplay reveal today as part of its Echoes of Central Park showcase, giving us our first substantial look at the expansion following its announcement at Gamescom.

The timing could be a risky move for Ubisoft, putting Echoes of Central Park just two days ahead of an all-time classic getting a major remake — though the two games could be targeting audiences different enough that both have room to succeed.

Echoes of Central Park will finally make Central Park an explorable location in The Division series. The park was used as a mass burial ground during the original outbreak, and years later, it has become an overgrown and ominous place surrounded by rumors about what might be lurking inside.

articles.title: Experimental RPG developer Summer Eternal: 'We're giving away 5% of our studio to you, the Players' in order to 'mend the trust broken in this industry a thousand times over'
articles.summary: Summer Eternal is an RPG studio co-founded by ex-ZA/UM designers Argo Tuulik and Dora Klindžić, as well as developer/organizer Aleksandar Gavrilović (quoted above). Given the former two developers' experience working on a canceled Disco Elysium expansion, it makes sense they'd want to try something…
body: Worker-owned cooperatives are rare but not unheard-of in games, but Summer Eternal is also looking to offer ownership stakes (and profit sharing) to its freelancers and customers. Crucially, it's not in the form of "walkin' around money" for the latter group. Instead, Summer Eternal wants to offer players a democratic say in the studio's direction, backed up by control of 5% of the profits.

It reminds me of the EVE Online Council of Stellar Management or Old School RuneScape's player voting on new features, but with this added element of the studio literally putting its money where its mouth is. At a time when traditionally governed, publicly-traded games companies are cannibalizing themselves before our eyes to fulfil a fiduciary duty to their shareholders, such an economically and politically radical proposition might have more broad appeal than it used to.

You can read Gavrilović's full posts on the governance of Summer Eternal and the profit-directing player non-profit on the studio's website. If you'd like to get in on the ground floor as a player-stakeholder, Summer Eternal's first product is actually a book.
